More people want tickets. A trend can fade. Fidget spinners are one example. When people lose interest, supply and demand can shift in a big way. Feelings Change What People Buy. Each person has different preferences. Each person has different values. Those differences change buying habits. That is why supply and demand keep moving the prices of goods and services. How buyers see a good also matters.

9How they see a service matters too. People often pay more for something they view as valuable. They pay more for something they view as cool. Each buyer does that math in a personal way. Personality shapes the choice. A budget shapes it too. Shoes can differ a great deal in price. The difference follows what buyers prefer. Plain sneakers are typically much cheaper than another kind. The other kind is tied to the name of a celebrity athlete. Some buyers see worth in that athlete's endorsement. They will pay extra for the celebrity link. Other buyers want the lowest price they can find. Every buyer is different. Personal values and personal situations make them so. Many styles of those famous athlete shoes have been sold since 1985. Your choices as a buyer can shift supply and demand. The Part You Play. By now you can see how often markets touch daily life. You take part in them. So does everyone you know. Pause and think about the goods your family buys often.

10Think about the services too. The next time one of those prices goes up or down, notice how you feel. Did your demand change because the price changed? Demand here means how much you wanted the item. Why would the new price change that want? You might buy candy. You might buy a house. Either purchase puts you in the push and pull of supply and demand. Words to Know. Demand: the need for a good or a service, or the wish for it. Endorsement: backing or approval of a product or a service, sometimes given in return for money. Fixed: not open to change. Fluctuate: to shift again and again. Influencing: having an effect on people or on things. Merchandise: things that are bought or sold. Product: a thing that is made, grown, or produced, most often so it can be sold. Supply: how much of something is on hand for sale or for use. Surplus: what remains after the amount people need has been met.

118. Wild Animals Kept as Pets

1A woman in Whittlebury, England, keeps three pet foxes. One of the foxes poses in its home. In the jungles of Ecuador, people often see wild parrots. Think about the wildest animals on Earth. Think about the most amazing ones. You might picture an African lion. You might picture a white tiger. You might picture an elephant. You might picture a big black bear. You may see them running across a savanna. High jungle branches may be where you picture them at rest. Zoos may already have brought you near them. Some people keep wild animals in their homes. They keep animals such as tigers. They keep parrots. They keep pythons. These pets are called exotic pets. A group of animal doctors in the United States made an estimate. They estimate that one in ten homes there has an exotic pet. Exotic means unusual. It can mean something from a faraway place. A home fox is one kind of surprising pet. Parrots in an Ecuador jungle show the wild life some people want nearby. Any of those four animals might be the picture that comes first. Zoos let people stand near animals that others keep at home. Law in the United States defines exotic animals in a certain way.

2They are animals not usually kept as pets. They are not usually kept on farms. Other countries are a common origin for them. Huge size is not required for an animal to count as exotic. Hedgehogs are considered exotic pets. Turtles are considered exotic pets. Gerbils are considered exotic pets. Lizards are considered exotic pets. Exotic animals are usually wild. Wild here means they have not been domesticated. Living easily with humans is what breeding shaped in a domestic animal. A dog is a domestic animal. A horse is a domestic animal. Gentle behavior is a common result of that breeding. Social behavior is another common result of that breeding. Survival in the wild is what their traits support. Because of that, they can be very dangerous as pets. Prey is what a wild cheetah runs after in Kenya. Kenya is in Africa. A ball is what a domestic dog runs after. Do not try to treat a wild animal like that dog. Everyday activities are where some owners place their exotic animals. Domesticated describes plants or animals raised for human use. Many exotic animals make fun pets. They become beloved pets. They can be beautiful to watch.

3They can be interesting to watch. Domestic animals can be those things too. A dog may not sound unusual. A fish may not sound unusual. A cat may not sound unusual. Amazement is what a tiger brings. Showing off is the goal for some owners of a wild pet. A cheetah can be that kind of pet. Other people have their own personal zoos. The next animal for a collection may be sought all over the world. Love for the animals is the simple reason for many owners. Family treatment is how some owners act toward them. Some owners dress certain animals in human clothes. Chimpanzees are one animal that gets dressed this way. Pet homes in the United States hold millions of exotic animals. More of them live as pets there than live in zoos. Big cats are among the most desired. Tigers are among those big cats. Lions are among them. Cheetahs are among them. Fifteen thousand primate pets live in the United States. Those pets include chimpanzees. They include monkeys. No exotic pet type is more common than reptiles. Tiny lizards are one end of that reptile range. Deadly snakes are the other end. American homes also keep exotic birds gathered from many lands.

4Tigers are so popular that a surprising count is true. Pet homes in the United States hold more tigers than the wild does worldwide. Zoos have fewer than one-tenth as many tigers as United States pet homes. Free-roaming tigers around the world number only about three thousand. Over five thousand live in homes in the United States. A pet tiger is a hard animal to care for. One tiger can add a lot to a family's grocery bill. Daily meat for one tiger can reach 9 kilograms (20 pounds). That is over 3,175 kilograms (7,000 pounds) of meat a year. Two tigers live at Stump Hill Farm. The farm is in Massillon, Ohio. One tiger is named Noah. The other tiger is named Layla. Many exotic pets are in the United States. China, though, buys more in the exotic pet trade than any other place. Owning a pet snake is popular there. Owning a pet crocodile is popular. Owning a pet monkey is popular. Owning a pet shark is popular. Some lands in the Middle East treat a pet cheetah as a sign of high rank. It is a symbol among very wealthy people. No other place brings in more pet reptiles than Europe.

5Asia supplies nearly half of the wildlife that is traded. Africa is the source that comes after Asia. After Africa come South America and Central America. Selling wildlife provides income that many communities need. Taking too many animals from the wild can threaten a species. A sofa is where one pet cheetah rests. The sofa is in an apartment in Kuwait. Importing is bringing goods in from elsewhere so they can be sold. Physically similar living things form a species. Members of a species can reproduce. Illegal exotic animals come from many places. South America is one source of monkeys. It is a source of jaguars. It is a source of piranhas. Africa is a source of cheetahs. It is a source of elephants. It is a source of rhinoceroses. Russia is a source of brown bears. It is a source of Amur tigers. It is a source of snow leopards. Southeast Asia and Australia are a source of parrots. They are a source of snakes. They are a source of kangaroos. These are only a few examples. Many more exotic animals are exported against the law. An agreement carries the signatures of nearly two hundred countries.

6The agreement is about endangered species. Endangered species are animals at risk of becoming extinct. The agreement sets rules to protect them from being traded. Buying an exotic pet can cost thousands of dollars. Caring for one can be expensive too. High cost means the buyers are often wealthy. Payment power is no promise of good treatment for the animal. Each state in the United States can set different exotic-pet laws. Any animal may be owned legally in some states. Other states do not allow certain animals. A special permit is required of owners in some states. Some animals are sold legally. The legal sales happen through auctions. They also happen through stores. Many other animals are bought and sold illegally. International borders may be crossed in secret with these animals. They may be hidden from authorities. Smugglers gain billions of dollars from this practice. The animals pay the price. They are packed into tight crates. They often have little food. The journey kills as many as 90 percent of them. In October 2017, authorities in Indonesia held a raid. That raid took over 100 pangolins classed as endangered. Extinct means no longer in existence. It means completely wiped out. Illegally means in a way the law forbids.

7Smuggled means moved in secret, against the law. A count of dangers covers the United States from 1990 to 2011. The count lists 28 for bears. It lists 9 for marine animals. It lists 52 for elephants. It lists 164 for big cats. It lists 58 for other animals. It lists 129 for primates. It lists 103 for reptiles. The total shown is 543. The page also lists 21 for big cats. It also lists 14 for elephants. It also lists 18 for reptiles. It also lists 16 for other animals. Owners can be in danger once these animals are taken in. Dozens of attacks on humans by exotic animals happen every year. The attacks cause injury. The attacks can even cause death. Baby animals are the ones often offered for sale. As babies they are gentle. As babies they are sweet. Growing older brings natural changes to many of them. One change can be a sudden wish to hunt. One change can be a sudden wish to escape. One change can be a sudden wish to find a mate. Those wishes can lead to aggressive behavior. Many owners are surprised. A pet that was friendly can turn vicious.

8Television has helped make exotic pets popular. Movies have helped. Social media has helped. A screen can make people want the animal they just watched. After movies showed a snowy owl, sales of that bird rose quickly. Many owners later find the animals too hard to care for. The pets are often abandoned. The pets are often neglected. A snowy owl that appeared in those movies has a wild home. The harsh Arctic tundra is the usual home of snowy owls. Aggressive means ready or likely to attack. It can also mean too forceful. Neglected means not properly cared for. It can mean ignored. The years 1990 to 2011 hold the danger counts above. A sweet baby animal can change as it grows. Another risk of an exotic pet is disease. The government of the United States reports a high share. Animals are the source of almost 75 percent of new human diseases. A pet can be the contact that spreads some of these illnesses. Salmonella is one example. It is a dangerous disease. It spreads from pet reptiles. About seventy thousand humans get it each year. Burmese pythons arrived in pet stores in the United States. Large numbers of customers made purchases.

9Many buyers did not know how big a baby could get. A python bought small can later reach 3.7 meters (12 feet) in length. It can weigh 113 kilograms (250 pounds). Many owners were overwhelmed. They turned the snakes loose. Some pythons reached the Florida Everglades. The Everglades are swampy. Over time, their numbers soared. Native species started to be pushed out by them. Rabbits were among those species. Deer were among them. Raccoons were among them. Payment for hunting these snakes started in the community in 2017. The snakes were invaders. A giant Burmese python is held by biologists in Florida. They are in Everglades National Park. The park is near Homestead, Florida. Lilly is an alligator. Lilly lives at home in Pennsylvania. Lilly has a tiara. Lilly has pink dresses. Lilly even gets her nails painted. People disagree about owning exotic animals. Any animal, some say, is a pet humans have a right to keep. Others believe the danger is too great a risk. The danger is to the animals. The danger is also to humans. Freedom, still others say, is a right that wild animals have. Happiness as a pet, they say, can never come to a wild animal.

10A loose python in a swamp shows one cost of the pet trade. Lilly's dresses show how some owners treat a wild animal like a person. Interest in exotic animals will not leave humans. Fun is how exotic-pet ownership can look. Animals can suffer great harm from that choice. Enjoyment of exotic animals can happen in other ways. Television is one place to watch them. We can watch them over the Internet. Those views show them roaming free where they naturally live. Visits are possible in places that supply what they need. Those places give them what they need to thrive. Watching is more fun if the animals are happy. It is more fun when they are healthy. Cars enclose the tourists on a South Africa safari. The wild animals roam free around the cars. A screen can show an animal in its own habitat. A well-run visit can give the animal what it needs. Happiness and health make the watching better. The cars on safari keep people inside while animals stay free. Interest in exotic animals does not have to mean owning one. The harm of keeping them can be large. Freedom in a real habitat is another way to see them.
